title: Compact density accessibility remediation and VPAT checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Scope: Audit and remediate accessibility regressions introduced by compact-density variants across tokens, buttons, tables and chart components; produce a VPAT-aligned checklist and remediation plan for design and engineering handoff.

Background: Compact density (reduced spacing/tightened touch targets) has been adopted in several dashboards to maximize information density. During an accessibility sweep, we found multiple issues in this mode that are not present in default density: (1) keyboard focus rings clipped or visually indistinct because padding was reduced without adjusting focus outline offsets, (2) table row/column headers missing explicit ARIA relationships when visual grouping is tight, causing screen reader users to lose contextual anchors, (3) contrast failures for thin line charts and heatmap cells at small sizes and in dark theme, and (4) buttons and toggle groups with reduced hit target sizes falling below recommended WCAG touch-size guidance.

Objectives:
- Produce a VPAT-friendly checklist that maps each WCAG and Section 508 requirement to component-level remediation (e.g., table headers, focus order, color contrast, target sizes).
- Implement design token adjustments (contrast ramp, focus offsets, min-touch tokens) that restore compliance while preserving compact visual density where possible.
- Deliver engineering-ready CSS patterns and React component updates to ensure keyboard-only and screen-reader flows are robust in compact mode.
- Validate fixes with automated checks (axe + custom color contrast thresholds) and manual QA across macOS VoiceOver, NVDA, and TalkBack on mobile density previews.

Trade-offs & decisions to make:
- Visual fidelity vs compliance: increasing stroke weight or cell padding could change perceived density. We'll prefer token-based contrast increases and focus-offset outlines before increasing spacing. If necessary, provide an alternate ‘dense-readable’ variant that slightly relaxes density for critical accessibility workflows.
- Theming constraints: some customers rely on dark theme density for dashboards. Proposed token changes must be scoped so they don’t break enterprise brand overrides. Recommend exposing a small set of density-accessibility tokens to Dedicated/Private deployments for customer overrides.

Links & artifacts:
- Audit doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/compact-density-a11y-audit-2025
- VPAT checklist draft (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/VPAT-compact-density-2025
- Engineering PR (prototype fixes): https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/1247
- Figma file (token proposals & visuals): https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/DS-density-a11y-2025

Handoff deliverables: design token patch, component CSS snippet examples, unit tests for focus-visible and keyboard nav, a11y regression test plan, and VPAT checklist with acceptance examples.
comments: 2025-03-11 - Asha Patel: Kickoff with PM and Eng. Collected initial audit notes; prioritized table header ARIA relationships and focus clipping as blockers for compact mode release.
2025-03-14 - Nora Kim: Completed token sketch: focus-offset token (+4px) and a contrast ramp for thin stroke colors. Shared Figma frames for review.

2025-03-16 - Engineering review (ENG-4982): Kernel constraints noted — some components cannot accept additional DOM wrappers due to virtualization performance. We must prefer CSS-only fixes where possible.
2025-03-18 - UX Research: Ran quick keyboard-only walkthroughs on 3 dashboards; found two more places where focus order diverged when compact spacing collapsed affordances.
2025-03-20 - Nora Kim: Pushed prototype PR for focus-offset and updated chart color palette. Requesting design review and a11y validation run (axe + manual). PR: #1247
2025-03-24 - Accessibility lead (Liam Carter): Reviewed contrast adjustments; recommended increasing heatmap cell min-luminance to 12% in dark theme to pass WCAG AA for non-text graphic objects.
2025-03-25 - Nora Kim: Updated VPAT checklist with mapping to WCAG 2.1 criteria and example acceptance steps. Marked table header ARIA fixes as highest priority for next sprint.
acceptance_criteria: All compact-density table variants expose programmatic header associations (aria-labelledby/aria-describedby or scope headers) and pass NVDA/VoiceOver header navigation tests.
Keyboard focus is never visually clipped in compact mode; focus-visible offset token applied and validated at small viewport widths.
Chart thin-line and heatmap contrast tokens meet WCAG AA non-text contrast guidance when used at production sizes in both light and dark themes.
Buttons and toggles in compact mode meet minimum target size or have an explicit a11y-label/hit-area extension implemented and documented.
VPAT checklist completed and attached to ticket; QA evidence (screenshots + test steps) included for each WCAG mapping.
